text.34630ffed84a41fc1262: Growth paths and maturity · Valuation Lab
text.5b41f00b0c29df763e90: Current-company research, October 17, 2026. A transparent set of analyst assumptions, not issuer guidance, a target-price fit or calibrated probabilities.
text.71d4f3ab9e4fd4c1ff5d: Choose the growth pattern and its duration
text.9e4dafb34672d5d61618: an immediate fade, the initial growth rate maintained for 3 or 5 years, or individually entered growth rates for years 1–3 or 1–5.
text.dacc3bb26c0ffbd3c0ed: year 10, 15 or 20. This controls revenue growth only. Profitability and capital-efficiency timing have separate inputs in their respective sections. For 3 explicit years and maturity at 10, there are 7 fade years. For 5 explicit years and maturity at 20, there are 15 fade years.
text.568d50d985f435232272: The legacy immediate-fade path remains the default with exactly its previous ten-year calculations and constant incremental sales/capital. Existing researched cases and historical freezes are unchanged. The AAOI staged capacity case keeps its documented ten-year schedule. Switching from the original model to an editable growth pattern establishes an explicit capital transition. Its initial profitability and capital-efficiency endpoints are year 10; subsequent growth edits leave those timings unchanged. Previously saved flexible paths keep their exact existing economics until edited.
text.adb13827b45bf5d5ca7a: Damodaran relates the high-growth period to company size, existing growth and competitive advantages. His firm-valuation chapter includes a Cisco example with six high-growth years followed by six transition years. The familiar five-year high-growth stage plus five-year transition is a modeling pattern, not a universal maximum. The duration still needs a business justification.
text.bcf0b197080816f8a368: Damodaran: length of the high-growth period
text.b79f7acdef8d87df0cf5: Closure in valuation: stable growth and terminal value
text.c5eb96ee8e71ca58c374: These controls implement a simplified, explicit transition. They do not reproduce every Damodaran model. Margin convergence, competitive advantages, capital productivity and risk can evolve on different schedules. The current editable profile gives growth, margin and capital efficiency independent timelines. The cash-flow forecast ends at the latest of those endpoints, so every mature assumption has been reached before terminal value begins. WACC is constant throughout, with no capital-structure or risk fade.
text.c042d53145d99d924401: Let G be growth maturity, E be 3 or 5 explicit years, and g be stable growth. Maintained growth uses the initial rate in years 1–E. Annual-entry mode uses the initial scalar in year 1 and the entered rates in years 2–E. Thereafter:
text.bc58ca7dc546bc61ac04: Flexible immediate fade uses initial growth in year 1 and reaches g in year G, using min(1, (year − 1)/(G − 1)). This follows the original growth timing, but its capital intensity transitions to maturity rather than staying constant. Neither immediate mode nor the explicit phases independently resample each future year.
text.c850de7995ae06f60347: The normalized starting EBIT margin converges linearly to the mature margin over M years, then stays at that margin. M is an independent input in Profitability. Taxes apply only to positive EBIT; no NOL ledger or automatic loss refund is assumed. WACC is the same scalar in every forecast year and in the terminal formula.
text.98f347ef3fb3fafa39e1: Capital intensity means new capital per unit of new revenue, the reciprocal of incremental sales/capital. It stays at its initial level through K, then transitions linearly to the terminal-consistent endpoint at C. K and C are independent inputs in Investment. Changing the growth pattern or its duration does not move them. A new immediate-fade profile initially sets K = 0; a new hold or annual-entry profile initially sets K to its explicit-growth length. After creation, the timing remains independent. No terminal ROIC is inferred from historical accounting ratios, and it is not automatically set equal to WACC.
text.0963cf96dd2bddfe01f2: The (1 + g) factor reconciles current-year incremental revenue with the protected engine’s next-year terminal NOPAT timing. With the final forecast year already at stable growth, mature margin and terminal-consistent intensity, FCFF(N) × (1 + g) equals terminal FCFF. A positive mature margin is required to derive finite terminal sales/capital. Stable growth must remain below both WACC and mature marginal ROIC.
text.300302859193cce42462: The reinvestment total shown in Growth is a modeled net-growth investment requirement. It is not a balance-sheet invested-capital forecast, a maintenance capex schedule or evidence that funding is available. Revenue declines do not automatically release assets. Revenue multiples are shown without inventing future market share.
text.e42b9f33eed7ec7d9d37: Why a longer growth period can still lower value
text.a39c3839037616f8e029: Extending revenue growth leaves margin and capital-efficiency schedules unchanged, but does not guarantee higher value. Extra sales still consume capital. Value depends on the return earned on that extra investment relative to its cost of capital; no monotonic-value adjustment is applied. The earlier coupled profile could also delay profitability and capital efficiency when its horizon increased. That coupling is preserved only for untouched saved version-1 calculations, and is removed by anchoring the separate timelines when the user edits growth.
text.8a3d232e058b98996193: Monte Carlo and explicit annual paths
text.477ffa6dbf6dbfc01a88: Each trial samples one vector: initial growth, mature margin, initial sales/capital and WACC. It then rebuilds the entire annual operating path with the same adapter used by deterministic valuation. For explicit-entry paths, every explicit growth rate shifts by the same percentage-point change between sampled initial growth and baseline initial growth; the fade still ends at fixed stable growth.
text.e885bda125b9994ac23c: This is a disclosed parallel-shift path assumption. It is neither independently resampled yearly growth nor fitted economic covariance. Other path shapes require analyst changes to the baseline. All maturity endpoints, the capital-transition start, explicit growth phase, tax, stable growth and terminal ROIC stay fixed within a trial. The capital-intensity endpoint is recalculated from that trial’s mature margin; additional revenue still requires additional reinvestment. WACC is drawn once and constant within that trial. Every explicit annual rate must stay between −50% and 200%; initial growth remains within the existing −50% to 100% scalar bound. Invalid trials are excluded without replacement or clipping, and the exclusions are reported.
text.cd469884db68524bc9f9: Original-model saved drafts keep their original ten-year behavior. Saved flexible schema-version-1 profiles keep the exact old coupled calculation on reload. An explicit growth edit upgrades that profile to schema version 2, first anchoring margin maturity and capital maturity at its old horizon and the capital-transition start at its old explicit-growth length. Only then is the requested growth change applied. For example, changing a saved 15-year growth path to 20 years retains year-15 margin and capital maturity. A saved 20-year path instead retains year-20 margin and capital maturity when growth is shortened. No prior case is silently recalculated. Malformed flexible saved inputs withhold results instead of being silently filled with research defaults. Loading research explicitly restores its original path; Undo load can restore the prior draft. Path Undo retains independent scalar, notes and claims edits; growth-duration Undo retains later annual-rate edits. Undo restores the prior version where possible; independently edited margin or capital timing is retained rather than silently discarded. Exports record both the growth endpoint and the actual cash-flow forecast length.
text.ef5ea0bd417b27c415d3: Independent numerical oracles cover the phase and horizon combinations, terminal reinvestment identity, seeded trial replay, invalid annual rates and legacy equivalence. Minimal DOM tests cover the actual input handlers, persistence, Undo, research loading and exports. Static document-renderer previews are layout approximations; authenticated real-browser, touch and screen-reader behavior remains unverified under the existing executor limits.
